stories.headline: A rare jaguar was photographed crossing a vital forest corridor
stories.summary: Panthera's camera traps caught a male jaguar in the corridor linking Guatemala and Honduras. Experts call photos like this a once-a-decade treat, proof big cats still use the route.
stories.why: Linked forests keep jaguar groups from becoming isolated and inbred.

stories.stat_label: years old, with its staircase intact
stories.headline: A 10th-century building turned up at Otto the Great's palace
stories.summary: Beside the royal palace at Helfta, diggers found a stone building with a cellar and a well-preserved staircase. Other finds include silver coins and an almost playable bone flute.
stories.why: Bit by bit, a lost emperor's palace is coming back to light.

stories.stat_label: handmade dolls for kids in need
stories.headline: 10 women, most over 70, knitted 567 dolls for children in need
stories.summary: Meeting monthly in Cape Town, the group knitted 567 IZZY Dolls with their own wool. 11 groups, including a cancer charity helping kids in chemo, will hand them out.
stories.why: A small doll to hold can comfort a frightened child.

stories.headline: The most distant radio flash ever traced was found with Webb
stories.summary: South Africa's MeerKAT caught a radio flash lasting milliseconds. A University of Sydney-led team used Webb to trace it to a tiny galaxy from when the universe was ~3 billion years old.
stories.why: It more than doubles the old record, opening a new window on the early universe.
